title: Runtime LTS patch canary + rollout plan (SRE)
content:
Owner: Miles (SRE)
Co-owners: Sean (gates/SLOs), Rafael (oncall + escalation)
Last reviewed with Release Eng: 2026-01-21

Purpose
- Define a repeatable, audit-friendly canary + rollout process for Runtime LTS patch releases (e.g., runtime-1.20-lts.1).
- Make patch promotion decisions predictable: what we watch, for how long, who gets paged, and when we roll back.
- Reduce enterprise customer risk for Dedicated/Private while keeping the patch cadence sustainable.

Non-goals
- This doc does NOT define backport eligibility (see Runtime LTS Backport Policy).
- This doc does NOT replace incident response. It links to the oncall playbook for LTS-related incidents.

Definitions (SRE view)
- Patch candidate / RC: A signed artifact built from the LTS branch and promoted to an RC channel for canary.
- Canary: A controlled slice of production traffic or deployments, running the new patch under enhanced monitoring.
- Promotion: Moving the patch from RC -> LTS stable channel (published image tags + release notes).
- Rollback: Reverting canary and/or stable to previous known-good patch. Rollback always includes a comms step.

Scope of rollouts
We currently have 3 deployment surfaces where LTS shows up:
1) Hosted API (Redwood-run multi-tenant clusters)
2) Dedicated (customer-isolated GPU pools in our infra)
3) Private (VPC/on-prem via installer/Helm; customer-operated)

This plan is written to cover Hosted + Dedicated canary as the default gating mechanism before we publish the LTS patch broadly. For Private, we treat our Hosted/Dedicated canary as the primary safety signal, then publish a Private-friendly artifact and guidance.

Pre-requisites (before canary begins)
1) Release Eng prerequisites
- Artifact provenance: signed image + attestation present (see CI/Provenance doc). No signature = no canary.
- Determinism checks: LTS reproducible build checks must pass.
- Changelog draft exists using LTS template (even if marked DRAFT) including risk level.

2) Runtime prerequisites
- Release notes include: any known behavior changes, feature flags touched, and “expected blast radius” summary.
- Runtime team has nominated an “LTS patch oncall buddy” for the canary window (usually Omar or Samir).

3) SRE prerequisites
- Canary dashboards are green for baseline (previous patch) within the last 24h.
- Canary alert routes are correct (see Paging policy section).
- Capacity headroom: we need enough spare GPU capacity to roll back fast without queueing collapse.

Canary stages (standard patch cadence)
Stage 0: Lab/Pre-prod validation (required)
- Owner: Sahana (CI) + Allison (signals)
- Duration: completes before RC is cut; not time-based.
- Inputs:
  - perf-canary suite (PR #311 baselines) against representative workloads
  - benchmark-lab dataset version pinning (see benchmark-lab PR #522)
- Pass criteria (relative to previous stable LTS patch):
  - p95 latency: <= +2%
  - p99 latency: <= +3%
  - throughput: >= -2%
  - error rate (5xx + runtime errors): no increase > 0.05% absolute
- Notes:
  - If the patch is explicitly a perf regression fix, Sean may approve adjusted deltas, but it must be called out in release notes.

Stage 1: Internal production canary (Hosted)
- Owner: Miles (execution) + Sean (go/no-go)
- Duration: 2 hours minimum, business hours preferred (but can run off-hours with explicit paging coverage).
- Rollout: enable RC on 1% of Hosted traffic in ONE region only.
- Region selection preference: start with us-east-1 (highest traffic, best signal) unless there is known region-specific risk.
- Routing method: policy-based routing on runtime image tag for the canary pool.
- Pass criteria (over the canary window):
  - No sustained error-rate increase > 0.1% absolute for 10 minutes
  - No sustained p95 > +3% for 10 minutes (vs baseline preceding 6h median)
  - No sustained p99 > +5% for 10 minutes
  - No increase in OOM kill events (node + container) > 1 per hour vs baseline
  - No increase in “queue wait time” p95 > +5% (guardrail to catch scheduling regressions)
- “Stop-the-line” failures (immediate rollback):
  - Any crash loop affecting > 10% of canary pods
  - Any data integrity issue suspected (token corruption, malformed streaming, tool/function calling protocol breaks)
  - Any security issue surfaced during canary (e.g., signature verification mismatch)

Stage 2: Multi-region production canary (Hosted)
- Owner: Miles
- Duration: 6 hours minimum (or 1 full diurnal peak window, whichever is longer, for patches touching scheduling/kernels)
- Rollout: 1% -> 5% traffic in 2 regions, then 10% traffic in 3 regions.
- Escalation: if any single region fails but others are clean, treat as “region-specific suspect” and pause expansion until investigated.
- Pass criteria:
  - Same as Stage 1, but evaluate per-region and global aggregate.
  - No increase in tail-latency spikes correlated with batch size distribution shifts.

Stage 3: Dedicated canary
- Owner: Rafael (customer-impact guardrails) + Miles
- Duration: 24 hours.
- Rollout: choose 2 dedicated pools (internal + one low-risk customer with explicit opt-in).
  - Internal dedicated pool: Redwood dogfood (preferred)
  - External: only if we have written opt-in and a rollback window agreed
- Pass criteria:
  - No customer SLO breaches attributable to runtime (error budget burn not exceeding 2x normal rate)
  - No increase in GPU utilization variance that causes queue instability
  - No increase in restart frequency

Stage 4: Promote to LTS stable
- Owner: Connor (release) + Sean (approval)
- Requirements:
  - All stages pass OR Sean explicitly approves a waiver (waivers must be documented in the release notes + audit evidence)
  - Release notes finalized with explicit risk level and “what to watch”
  - Artifacts published to LTS stable channel (images + checksums) with correct tags

Emergency patches (out-of-band)
Used for:
- Security fixes under embargo
- High-severity correctness bugs causing widespread incident risk
- Severe perf regression introduced in previous LTS patch

Differences from standard cadence:
- Canary can be shortened, but not eliminated.
- Minimum requirements:
  - Stage 0 + Stage 1 required
  - Stage 2 optional with Sean+Rafael sign-off
  - Dedicated canary optional if we have compelling Hosted signal and rollback confidence
- Comms:
  - If embargoed, follow restricted distribution list. Do not post public-facing details until approved.

What we monitor (dashboards + key signals)
Primary dashboards (Grafana)
- Runtime LTS Canary Overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/lts-canary-overview
- Token Latency (p50/p95/p99) by model + region: https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/token-latency
- Error breakdown (5xx, timeouts, runtime exceptions, OOM): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/runtime-errors
- Scheduler health (queue depth, queue wait, batch size dist): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/scheduler-health
- GPU metrics (utilization, memory, throttling, ECC): https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/gpu-fleet-health

Logs/Tracing
- Loki search: runtime image tag + “panic|OOM|illegal memory access|cuda error”: https://loki.redwoodinference.net
- Traces: canary route sampling 5% during Stage 1/2 for latency attribution (request->scheduler->kernel): https://trace.redwoodinference.net

Golden signals we treat as promotion blockers
- Elevated tail latency without corresponding throughput benefit
- Increased queue wait time (often indicates scheduling regressions)
- Any increase in GPU OOMs or fragmentation causing thrash
- Increased retry rate or client disconnects during streaming

Baseline and comparison methodology
- Baseline is previous stable LTS patch, using:
  - preceding 6 hours median during similar traffic pattern (same weekday/time window if possible)
  - plus perf-canary suite results for controlled comparison
- We avoid comparing against “mainline” runtime because LTS is expected to be different (slower change).

Rollback criteria (clear triggers)
Immediate rollback (no debate, page Release Eng + Runtime)
- Error rate (5xx + runtime exceptions) > +0.3% absolute for 5 minutes in canary pool
- p99 latency > +10% for 10 minutes AND correlated to runtime tag (not upstream)
- Crash loop / repeated SIGSEGV / illegal memory access in canary pool
- Any suspected correctness regression (bad outputs, malformed tokenization, protocol breaks)
- Signing/attestation verification failure in production pipeline

Planned rollback (pause + assess, but default to rollback unless clear external cause)
- p95 latency > +5% for 15 minutes
- queue wait p95 > +10% for 15 minutes
- OOM kill rate > 2x baseline for 30 minutes
- GPU ECC error spikes correlated with new kernel path (requires hardware triage; still rollback the software to avoid churn)

Rollback steps (operator checklist)
1) Pause rollout automation (don’t let it expand traffic while debugging)
2) Shift canary traffic back to last known-good LTS patch tag
3) Validate recovery:
   - error rate back within baseline band
   - p95/p99 back within baseline band
   - queue depth stabilizes (no sustained growth)
4) Open incident (if customer-visible) and attach:
   - release tag
   - time of rollback
   - dashboard snapshots
5) Notify #eng-releases + #eng-runtime + #eng-sre with a 5-line summary and next step

Paging policy + escalation
During Stage 1/2 (Hosted canary)
- Primary pager: SRE oncall (Rafael rotates, but follow current schedule)
- Secondary: Runtime oncall buddy (Omar/Samir)
- Tertiary: Release Eng (Connor)
- Paging rules:
  - Page immediately on any “Immediate rollback” trigger
  - Otherwise, alert to Slack channel #eng-sre-canary (non-page) for trend warnings (p95 drift, minor error increase)

During Stage 3 (Dedicated canary)
- Primary pager: SRE oncall
- Secondary: Dedicated operations oncall (if separate rotation is active)
- Escalate to Product (Lauren) only if:
  - customer SLO impact is likely > 30 minutes OR
  - rollback requires coordination with customer change window

Customer comms guardrails (SRE input)
- For Dedicated/Private customers, we should avoid “silent behavior changes”. If we waive a gate, we must disclose:
  - what changed
  - why it’s safe
  - what to monitor
- If rollback occurred after any external customer exposure:
  - Support (Dev Patel / Owen Phillips) must get a short internal FAQ within 2 hours

Release-day staffing expectations
- Standard patch: at least 1 SRE (Miles or Rafael) available during Stage 1/2 execution window.
- Scheduling/kernel-touching patches: add Runtime lead (Sofia or Hiro) on standby.
- Emergency patch: explicit go/no-go signoff from Sean + Connor.

Notes / open questions
- Should we require a minimum 1-hour canary during peak traffic (as opposed to any 2 hours)? Suggest yes for scheduler changes.
- For Private: do we want a “customer canary ring” program (opt-in) similar to Dedicated? Product to confirm appetite.
- Need final URLs for “LTS stable artifact registry” and “RC artifact registry” once CI/Provenance doc lands.

Appendix A: Quick copy/paste canary announcement template (internal)
Subject: Starting Runtime LTS canary: <runtime-1.xx-lts.y-rc1>
- Scope: Hosted <region(s)>, <1%->5%->10%>
- Duration: <planned window>
- Primary dashboards: <links>
- Rollback triggers: error rate +0.3% / p99 +10% / crashes / correctness
- Oncall: SRE <name>, Runtime buddy <name>, Release Eng <name>

Appendix B: Minimal evidence we attach for audit
- RC artifact digest + signature verification proof
- Links/screenshots: Stage 0 perf suite, Stage 1/2 dashboards, decision timestamp
- Approval trail: Sean (gates) + Connor (release) in #eng-releases thread
